subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Oct 1-2 invoice — timestamp/attribution question
messages:
From: Trevor Lang <trevor.lang@brightlane.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Spike on Oct 1-2 invoice — can you explain?

Ben —

Hope you had a good weekend. We just got the October invoice and there is a ~420% increase in billed tokens for Oct 1–2 compared to our usual baseline. I attached the invoice to this note (invoice-2026-10-01.pdf).

We understand usage can fluctuate, but:
- The spike starts at 23:50 UTC on Oct 1 and drops at 00:10 UTC Oct 2 — a very narrow window.
- Our app had no feature release at that time and all internal teams report normal traffic.

Can you: (1) share the raw usage export for that window, (2) check for any attribution changes / timezone shifts on your end, and (3) let us know if this is billable or if we should expect an adjustment?

This is blocking our AP team from releasing payment for the month. Appreciate a fast turnaround.

Thanks,
Trevor Lang
Lead Finance Ops — BrightLane Health
accounts-payable@brightlane.com

Attachment: invoice-2026-10-01.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Trevor Lang <trevor.lang@brightlane.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spike on Oct 1-2 invoice — can you explain?

Trevor —

Thanks for flagging this and for attaching the invoice. I'm looking into it now. Two quick notes:

1) We'll generate a per-request export for Oct 1 22:00 UTC — Oct 2 02:00 UTC and share it as a CSV (token-level, request timestamps, route/model).
2) There's been one scheduled upgrade to our ingestion service this quarter that adjusted a millisecond timestamp normalization. It's unlikely to create a 400% jump, but it can shift a few thousand requests across the UTC day boundary if sessions were open around midnight.

I'm looping in Monica (billing reconciliation) so she can pull the canonical logs and run attribution. Expect the export within business hours Monday morning (my time). If we find the spike is due to our side (timestamp normalization or duplicated ingestion), we'll propose an adjustment.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Billing Team <billing@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Spike on Oct 1-2 invoice — BrightLane (RDW-DEAL-7841)

Forwarding BrightLane's request — they report a concentrated spike centered on 2026-10-01 23:50 UTC. Monica, can you pull: (A) the per-request export for 2026-10-01T22:00:00Z -> 2026-10-02T02:00:00Z (include request_id, timestamp_utc, model, route, token_in, token_out, attribution_id), and (B) any service-deployment logs around Oct 1 23:00–01:00 UTC for ingestion/edge.

Notes from my side: there was a non-disruptive ingestion normalization on Oct 1 (2026-10-01T22:45Z) that switched to millisecond-aligned timestamps. Hypothesis: long-lived sessions with rolling streaming produced requests that now map to the next UTC minute because of rounding; for a few high-volume customers this can push counts across the boundary. We need concrete evidence before offering adjustments.

Please include a CSV stub and a short explanation we can send to the customer. If the spike is >20k tokens attributable to our change, recommend a one-time credit and note the process to avoid recurrence.

Thanks — Ben

Subject: Re: Spike on Oct 1-2 invoice — timestamp/attribution question

Trevor —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the per-request export for the window you requested (redwood-usage-export-20261001-20261002.csv) and a short reconciliation:

Summary:
- Total additional billed tokens in the Oct 1 23:50 — Oct 2 00:10 UTC window: 18,420 tokens above baseline.
- Root cause: our ingestion normalization performed at 2026-10-01T22:45:00Z introduced millisecond alignment which, for ~2.2% of streaming sessions, shifted the attributed timestamp forward by 30–80 seconds. Because BrightLane's traffic pattern has persistent streaming through the UTC boundary, ~63% of the shifted requests moved into Oct 2's bucket instead of Oct 1.
- There is no evidence of duplicate request ingestion or replay.

Proposed remediation:
1) One-time billing adjustment: credit for 100% of the 18,420 tokens (~$12.86 based on plan rates). We can apply the credit to your next invoice immediately.
2) Engineering follow-up: we will backfill attribution in the historical ledger for customers with consistent streaming patterns to ensure boundary-shifted requests are attributed to the original session start day (we expect a small ledger update).

I've attached an adjustment proposal PDF with the credit calculation and how it will be applied (adjustment-proposal-20261019.pdf). If that's acceptable, Ben can confirm and I'll push the credit.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Billing Reconciliation Lead — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-usage-export-20261001-20261002.csv, adjustment-proposal-20261019.pdf
